subject: Clarify heartbeat vs burst tokens and streaming SLA
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma@clearcart.com>, Ryan Lopez <ryan@clearcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify heartbeat vs burst tokens and streaming SLA

Hi Emma / Ryan —

Thanks again for the deep dive earlier. Quick recap from my side and a short list of clarifying questions so we can finalize a throughput sizing recommendation: 

What I heard (please correct anything):
- You have a baseline interactive path (web + mobile) that averages ~12 req/s during business hours; each request is typically ~700–900 tokens (model: open-llama-70b-q4*).
- You see burst windows up to ~70–90 req/s for 60–120s during promotional traffic.
- You also run long-lived streaming sessions (chat-like flows) with variable concurrent streams; you reported spikes of a few hundred concurrent streams in the busiest hour.
- Your latency target for non-streaming responses is p95 <= 300ms and for streaming p95 <= 500ms.

Clarifying asks (so we can map to SLOs and capacity):
1) Can you confirm median and 95th percentile tokens per request (we want explicit numbers for baseline vs outliers)?
2) What is the sustained (10-min window) tokens/sec baseline we should size for vs the 1–2 min crest tokens/sec?
3) For streaming sessions: what’s the average messages/sec per stream and the typical RTT between client message and first token?
4) Do you have a single global region or do you split traffic between us-east and us-west? Which region should we prioritize?
5) Can you share a 24–72h traffic snapshot (anonymized) with timestamps, request type (interactive/stream), tokens_in/out, and concurrency? Attach format works fine.

What we propose initially (pending answers):
- Modeling approach: steady-state baseline + token-bucket crest model; recommend a dedicated pool sized for baseline with a burst buffer (autoscale / queued burst capacity) for short crests.
- Canary: 2-week canary with continuous tracing + token-level cost telemetry, three-minute rolling windows for crest detection.
- SLOs: map p95 latency to request types and add a forced fallback policy to a lower-cost model if we detect sustained saturation for >5min.

Next steps:
- If you can send the anonymized snapshot (CSV) and confirm tokens/request numbers, I’ll run a quick capacity model and send a short DC (delta) sizing doc by EOD Wednesday.
- Optional: schedule a 30-min follow-up to walk the model outputs and canary plan.

Attachments: clearcart_traffic_snapshot.csv (example format), redwood_slo_matrix.pdf (proposal template).

Thanks — talk soon.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
http://redwood.ai

From: Emma Stone <emma@clearcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ryan Lopez <ryan@clearcart.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify heartbeat vs burst tokens and streaming SLA

Thanks, Evelyn — appreciated the clear summary. Answers inline below and I attached a short telemetry export.

- Median tokens/request: 760
- p95 tokens/request: 1,450 (we see long prompts for some power users)
- Sustained 10-min baseline tokens/sec (business hours, PST): ~8,500 tokens/sec
- Short crests (1–2 min): up to ~66,000 tokens/sec (this corresponds to ~80 req/s at peak request sizes)
- Streaming: average 0.8 messages/sec per active stream; concurrent streams peaked at ~320 during our last promo; typical first-token RTT target is 400–600ms from the app.
- Region: single region for now (us-west / us-west-2).

Attached: clearcart_telemetry_may.csv — 72h window anonymized. We also exported a small sample of streaming session counts per minute.

We can prioritize us-west for the canary. We are OK with a two-week canary.

Let me know if you need additional fields.

—Emma
Emma Stone
Director of ML Infrastructure, ClearCart Inc.

Attachment: clearcart_telemetry_may.csv (CSV, 72h sample)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Emma Stone <emma@clearcart.com>, Ryan Lopez <ryan@clearcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify heartbeat vs burst tokens and streaming SLA

Great — thanks for the numbers and the CSV, that’s exactly what we needed. Preliminary notes after a quick pass: 

- Baseline sizing: the 8,500 tokens/sec steady state maps to roughly 8 Nvidia-A10 equivalent inference units for the model family we discussed when factoring in streaming KV cache overhead.
- Burst buffering: to cover the 66k tokens/sec 90–120s crest we recommend a burst buffer configured to allow a short autoscale spike (cloud-backed burst capacity) plus a queue policy that prevents sustained QoS loss for >3min.
- Streaming concurrency: 320 concurrent streams with 0.8 messages/sec is load-light per stream but the aggregate KV cache and memory footprint matters; we recommend reserving persistent memory and segregated stream handling to avoid eviction-induced latency spikes.

Action items I’ll take on:
- I’ll produce a short sizing note (sizing_notes_05-12.txt) describing the recommended baseline cluster (GPU counts), burst policy options, and an estimated cost delta for a two-week canary. Expect that doc by EOD today.
- Draft a canary plan that includes sampling rules for streaming latency (first-token p50/p95) and token-level cost alerts.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min call Wed 13 May 10:00am PT to walk the sizing note and canary gating criteria. If that works for you I’ll send a calendar invite.

Evelyn
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sizing_notes_05-12.txt
